stem:
Nitin must report how many chairs to buy for $47$ guests when chairs are sold only in packs of $10$. He also has a separate tally that must record the exact guest count.

Which claim fits each need?

options.text: Call both answers "approximate value" only, without choosing exact, round-up, round-down, or nearest-place for each need.
Say that writing a rounded chair count is what creates the exact guest tally of $47$, instead of keeping the tally exact because that need requires exactness.
Buy $50$ chairs (round up in packs of $10$ so every guest has a seat) and keep $47$ exact in the guest tally.
Decide only by asking whether $47$ feels "big" or "small" in everyday talk, without using exact versus round-up/round-down/nearest-place for these two needs.

teacher.key_rationale: Packs of $10$ force a round-up to $50$ chairs so every guest is seated, while the guest tally must stay exact at $47$. Naming only "approximate value", reversing round and exact, or swapping in a big/small feel test all miss that hinge.
